transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's nice to meet you too. Well, what brings me in is that I just can’t seem to turn off the worrying once it starts. It's frustrating because I'll tell myself, you know, I’ve made the list, I've checked the dates, and I’ve done all I reasonably can to take care of things. But my mind just keeps going and going anyway.
When the worrying starts, do the thoughts feel intrusive and unwanted, like they pop into your mind even when you don’t want them to?

I wouldn't really say they pop into my mind out of nowhere. It's not quite like that. It's more that... well, I'll start thinking about something normal, like an upcoming trip or a household chore, and I just can't let it go. 

I do want to stop worrying about it, but the thoughts don't really feel like they're intruding from the outside, if that makes sense. They're just my own regular thoughts that get kind of stuck.
Do you find yourself worrying about many different parts of your life, rather than mainly one specific problem?

Yes, it's definitely a lot of different things. It's not just one big problem I'm focused on. My mind just keeps roaming from one thing to the next. Like, I'll be worrying about the schedule for an upcoming art exhibition I'm helping with, and then it shifts to my daughter's travel plans, and then I'm suddenly stressing about whether the house gutters need fixing. It's just... all these small things start to feel as if they could unravel into something much bigger, and it just hops from one topic to another.
Have you been worrying like this on most days for at least six months?

Yes, it's been most days. I'd say it's been going on for about seven months now. It started shortly after a good friend of mine passed away, and I was trying to keep the community projects we worked on together moving forward. Since then, the worrying just hasn't really stopped.
Do you feel that most of your worrying is mainly about your friend's death and the responsibilities that came after it?

Well, no, I wouldn't really say that. It definitely started around that time, and it was a very stressful period, but the worries themselves aren't really focused on my friend's passing or those specific projects anymore. 

It's... well, like I was saying before, it's just everyday things now. The house, my family, just normal day-to-day stuff. It's almost like the worrying just stuck around and attached itself to everything else, rather than staying focused on what originally triggered it.
When you start worrying, do you find it hard to control or stop the worry?

Yes, very hard. Actually, that's really what brings me in to see you today. I just can't seem to turn off the worrying once it starts. 

I try to be logical about it... I'll tell myself that I've already made the list, I've checked the dates, and I've done all I reasonably can to handle whatever it is. But even knowing all that, I just can't get my mind to stop. It just keeps going.
Do you often feel physically tense, like your muscles are tight or knotted?

Yes, I do. By the time evening rolls around, my shoulders and neck are just... they're so tight. I think I spend the whole day sort of holding myself braced, if that makes sense. I even catch myself clenching my jaw while I'm just sitting there trying to read, or when I'm planning out activities for the garden center. It's just this constant physical tightness.
Do you find that you get tired easily?

Yes, I do. Even if I manage to sleep through the whole night, I wake up feeling like I've already worked half a day. Just doing simple things, like watering the garden beds or sorting out papers for my book club... by the time I'm done with that, I just need to sit down and gather myself. It's really tiring.
Have you been feeling more irritable than usual?

No, I haven't really noticed that. I don't think I've been snapping at anyone or feeling unusually short-tempered. I mean, I get a little frustrated with myself sometimes because I can't just relax, but I wouldn't say I'm irritable with other people. It's really just the worrying and the physical exhaustion I mentioned.
Do you have trouble concentrating because of the worry?

No, I wouldn't say I have trouble concentrating. I can still focus fine when I'm reading my books for the club or going over my garden plans. The worry is there, but it doesn't really stop me from paying attention to what I'm doing.
